issue.title: 🐛 fix(chat): keep composer uploads per conversation
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Type a message and attach an image in a conversation without sending, then start a new conversation: the text is gone but the image is still in the new composer. The text is not actually lost. It is saved as a draft under the old conversation and restored when you switch back. The image stays because composer uploads lived in one global `chatUploadFileList`, which no switch ever cleared.

This keys the upload list by conversation, the same way text drafts and context selections already work:

- **Store**: `chatUploadFileList` → `chatUploadFileListByContext`. All upload actions and selectors now take the composer's context key (`messageMapKey(context)`, the same key `draftKey` and `contextSelectionKey` use). Empty buckets are dropped.
- **Composer**: the ChatInput store gets an optional `uploadContextKey`, which defaults to `contextSelectionKey`. `useChatInputUpload` / `useChatInputUploadKey` feed the upload buttons, the + menu, paste, file chips (remove/retry), Clear, and the mobile preview.
- **Other entry points** pass the key of the conversation they target: drag-and-drop zones on each conversation surface, Home, project home, restore-to-input, queued-message edit, the browser sidebar screenshot, and image markup → chat (the composer draft bus now publishes the attached composer's key).
- **Send from a blank conversation**: the call sites that moved context selections from the `_new` key to the minted topic now call `moveChatComposerAttachments`, which moves uploads too. These are in-place replacements, so `conversationLifecycle` and `gateway` do not grow. Progress from an in-flight upload follows its chip if the chip was moved.

Behavior notes:

- Home uses one stable upload key (`'home'`). Its text survives mode and agent switches, so attachments do too.
- A composer without any context key (the create-agent modal) no longer accepts uploads. That modal never sent attachments, and they used to leak into the next chat.
- The browser sidebar screenshot button is disabled when there is no writable composer to receive the image.

#### Test

- [ ] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

Existing tests were updated to the keyed API. Regression tests were added for: per-conversation upload isolation, moving staged attachments to a new key, an in-flight upload moved while a same-named file is staged under the old key, and the image-markup handoff when the user switches threads within a topic. Each new test fails without its fix. Checks run:

- `bun run check`: lint passes, 302 related tests pass.
- Vitest over `src/store/chat/slices/agentRun`, `src/features/{Conversation,ChatInput,Home,Projects}`, `src/components/DragUploadZone`, `src/store/file`: 4969 pass. The 1 failure (`ChatInput/store/action.test.ts`, plain-text paste) also fails on `canary`.
- `bun run type-check`: no new errors.

- Acceptance: Pending. The author will verify on the real product before merge: (1) type text and attach an image, start a new conversation → the composer is empty; (2) switch back → text and image are both restored; (3) send with an image from a blank conversation → no image left behind in the new topic or in the next blank conversation.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None found.

issue.title: 📝 docs: retell the README features as the super-agent onboarding story
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Rewrites the product description and the **Features** section of `README.md` and `README.zh-CN.md` to follow the new lobehub.com homepage story: one agent, Lobe AI, from its first day on the team until it passes its review.

- **Tagline**: "Super-Agents on Your Team", with the homepage hero line under it. The old `<sup>Your Chief Agent Operator</sup>` line is removed.
- **Features as a story**:
  - It opens like the homepage section: "From new hire to one of the team", one line under it, and four traits in a 2×2 grid (flexible access, parallel work, finds its own work, gets more expert). The chapters follow: `Day 1` Welcome to the team, `Week 1` Its first task (picks it up, hands it in, reports back), `Month 1–2` Settling in as the team grows, and `Month 3` It passes its review.
  - Each chapter has a short intro and the homepage cards for that chapter. A centered "Bring them onto your team" block closes the section.
  - The old Operator / Create / Collaborate / Evolve sections and their images are gone.
- **New images**: 16 webp images (the story cards in English, `.zh-CN` variants with the Chinese card copy, and the new "Super-Agents on Your Team" banner). They were captured from the homepage story cards (light theme, final frame, 2x) and uploaded to the LobeHub CDN (`hub-apac-1.lobeobjects.space/blog/assets/<md5>.webp`) with the landing repo's CDN uploader, so nothing binary lands in this repo.
- **Links**: both READMEs point at the CDN URLs, so the images render the same before and after merge.
- **TOC**: both TOCs are updated.

Also refreshes the sections below Features, using the lobehub.com site source and the self-hosting docs in this repo:

- **🧩 Marketplace** replaces the old 🧩 Plugins section (Function Calling plugins, plugin SDK and gateway). It covers Agents, MCP servers, Skills and AI / LLM icons, with their marketplace copy, and explains how to publish to each: agents from their settings plus the Creator Reward Program, MCP servers via `publish-mcp/skill.md` or `@lobehub/market-cli`, skills via a GitHub repo.
- **🛳 Self Hosting**:
  - Docker Compose comes first, as in `docs/self-hosting/start`: three commands, with a one-line list of what `setup.sh` starts.
  - The one-click deploy buttons stay. The Vercel button now asks for `APP_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `KEY_VAULTS_SECRET`, `AUTH_SECRET` and `JWKS_KEY` instead of `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
  - The environment variable table and the OpenAI sign-up walkthrough are gone. Configuration now lives in the Documentation table (environment variables, model providers, auth).
  - The AIHubMix third-party gateway entry is removed.
- **📖 Documentation** (new, before Self Hosting): a table of the main lobehub.com docs pages and what each covers. It lists getting started, Lobe AI, agents, agent team, external agents, tasks, memory, pages, resources, channels, Messenger, GitHub integration, marketplace, model providers, self-hosting, environment variables, auth and development. The zh README links the `/zh` docs. The old Ecosystem section is removed.
- **Local development** uses `bun run` for scripts, as in AGENTS.md.
- **Contributing**: "submit plugin" becomes "publish MCP".
- **🔬 Research** replaces More Products and matches the site's Research menu: MCPMark, the research paper on Hugging Face, and EVAL SYS.
- The zh README gains the RepoCloud deploy button it was missing.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] Added/updated tests
- [x] No tests needed

- Acceptance:
  - Rendered both Features sections with the GitHub Markdown API (`gh api markdown`), pointed the images at the local files, and checked full-page screenshots at GitHub's README width.
  - Checked every in-page link (18 per README after the TOC update) against `github-slugger` heading ids, and checked that every reference-style link has a definition. Nothing is missing.
  - The pre-commit hook passed: remark, prettier and the file-size gate.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None.

### AI assistance

- Harness: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK), version unknown
- Model: claude-opus-5-5
- Thinking level: unknown
- Division of work:
  - The AI wrote the README copy in both languages, captured and converted the images, and ran the checks.
  - The copy and images follow the lobehub.com homepage story, which the author reviewed in the landing repo.
  - Human review of this PR is pending.
- Implementation rationale:
  - The README now tells the same story as the homepage, so the images are the homepage cards themselves; they keep the card titles and match its chapter structure.
  - The images live in `docs/readme/` and load by raw URL, as the author asked. That location is only temporary until they move to the CDN.
- Verification: see Test above. All 16 CDN URLs return 200 with byte-identical content.

comment.body: @codex review

Fixed in b22ef7239e. Dropped the id-based bucket lookup. Each in-flight upload now records the key its chip lives under, and `moveChatUploadFileList` updates that record on move (even before the chip is added). Status updates dispatch to the recorded key, so a same-named upload staged later under the old key keeps its own updates.

Fixed in b6d6330146. Queued messages are now backed up to `localStorage` per identity scope (`src/store/channel/outboxStorage.ts`) when they are queued. They are removed only when the server confirms the send or the user deletes the message. On mount the conversation restores them (`restoreOutbox`, once per scope) as **Not sent**, because whether an interrupted send landed is unknown. Retry reuses the stored request key, so a send that did land is not stored twice. Covered by `outboxStorage.test.ts` and new cases in `action.queueSend.test.ts`. The PR description is updated to match.

Fixed in b5f2b54c0c. The thread-follow continuation (scope, location and mount guards) is now the `useFollowSent` hook, and `ChannelConversation` runs both the first send and Retry through it: `OutgoingStatus` takes an `onRetry` prop instead of calling `retrySend` itself. A main-conversation reply to an Agent that succeeds on Retry now opens its thread. Covered by `useFollowSent.test.ts`.

issue.title: ✨ feat(channel): send Channel messages optimistically
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Sending in a Channel used to lock the composer until the send request **and** the detail/list refreshes finished: the attach icon dimmed, Send spun, and the editor became read-only. This PR makes main-conversation and thread sends optimistic:

- The input clears at once and stays usable. You can keep typing, attach files, and send several messages in a row.
- The message appears in the timeline immediately, marked **Sending…**. It is replaced by the stored message once a refreshed latest page contains it.
- A failed send stays in place, marked **Not sent**, with **Retry** and **Delete**. Retry reuses the same request key, so the server stores the message at most once.
- One conversation's messages reach the server in order, through a per-conversation queue.
- Also removes the hint line shown under the reply target in the composer ("Continue in a thread …", "Quote only …"), along with its now-unused locale keys and the composer's `threadId` prop.

Implementation: an `outbox` in the Channel store (`src/store/channel/outbox.ts`), backed up to `localStorage`, with `queueSend` / `retrySend` / `discardSend`. A detail-replica `onApplied` effect settles sent entries. `ChannelConversation` merges outbox entries into the timeline and renders `OutgoingStatus`. `Composer` takes exactly one of `onQueue` (optimistic) or `onSend` (awaited).

#### Key Decisions / Non-goals

- **A failed message stays in the timeline instead of going back into the input** (product decision). Restoring it into the input would conflict with anything typed while the request was in flight.
- **Unsent messages survive a reload.** Sending and failed messages are kept in `localStorage` per identity scope (`outboxStorage.ts`), like a composer draft, and removed once the server confirms them or the user deletes them. After a reload they come back as **Not sent**, because whether an interrupted send landed is unknown; Retry reuses the request key, so it stores the message at most once.
- **The first message of a draft thread still waits for the server.** The thread does not exist until that send creates it. A send that @mentions people from outside the Channel also waits until their invites resolve.
- A queued send whose identity/workspace scope changed before its turn is never sent under the new identity. It is marked failed in its own scope, so it can be retried after switching back.
- **Known edge:** if the server stores a message but the response is lost, the stored copy and a **Not sent** copy show together. Retry returns the stored copy under the same request key. This is documented next to `settleOutbox`.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests

- `bun run check`: lint clean, 60 related tests pass. New `outbox.test.ts` and `action.queueSend.test.ts` cover: shows as sending before the server answers, settles once refreshed, a failed send retries under the same key, a deleted send is not sent, in-order delivery, and no send under a replaced identity.
- Type-check: no errors in the changed code.

- Acceptance: https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/ea78a027-3c8a-4750-8439-cdddcb44283a. Two rounds, all checks pass on a local full-stack run.
  - Round 1 (8/8): composer no longer locks, with before/after against base `679c83e710`; Sending → stored; in-order sends; failure with Retry and Delete, stored once; attachments while sending; reply header without the hint; zh-CN status text.
  - Round 2 (5/5, on `a52b916a92` after the rebase): a failed or interrupted send survives a reload as Not sent; Retry stores it once; Delete stays gone after a reload; the feed keeps following new messages while a failed one is last; regression of the optimistic send.
  - Not covered: Agent-message variants (reply-header hint, Retry opening the Agent's thread), because no Agent could be added in that environment. The sending→sent transition is evidenced by 30 ms sampling, not video.

Contribution source: AI-assisted

- Replace the `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` headline with retry-first guidance instead of claiming that the bound device is no longer registered. A missing live connection can also occur during reconnection.
- Add a dedicated `DeviceNotFound` chat error and English / Simplified Chinese copy, so the Web error card no longer suggests configuring the server gateway for this case.
- Map `DeviceNotFound` in Bot replies with retry-first English / Simplified Chinese guidance, while retaining the Operation ID and keeping raw gateway details out of channel messages.
- Preserve Goal failure classification for previously persisted headlines. Dispatch and retry behavior are unchanged; existing stored chat errors are not rewritten.

Screenshots are not available: the local sign-in prerequisite blocked the before/after UI check. Product acceptance remains incomplete.

issue.title: ✨ feat(device): update the CLI on every workspace device at once
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Workspace devices are often shared team machines, and keeping `lh` up to date meant opening each device and updating its CLI one by one. This adds an **Update CLIs** action to the workspace device list that updates every CLI in the current tab (Workspace pool or the caller's Private devices) in one pass, built on the existing single-device remote maintenance (`checkCliUpdate` / `restartCli`).

**Server** (`device` router, workspace-only)

- `checkCliUpdates({ visibility })` checks every CLI device in the tab that the caller may operate and returns a per-device plan. Nothing restarts.
- `updateClis({ targets })` checks each planned device again and restarts only the ones that are still idle and behind, under a caller-supplied `requestId` per device (idempotent retry on the device). Results come back per device: `requested` / `upToDate` / `busy` / `inProgress` / `unsupported` / `offline` / `failed`.
- Same permission as a single-device update (`canOperateWorkspaceDevice`). A target the caller cannot operate, or a gateway-only connection without a registry row, fails without any RPC reaching it.
- Devices are contacted with bounded concurrency (8). One debug log line records who triggered a batch and its outcome counts.

**Client** (`src/features/DeviceManager/CliBatchUpdate/`)

- A toolbar button, shown only when the caller can operate at least one CLI device in the tab, opens a modal with one state machine: checking → plan → sending → following → done.
- The plan lists every device with its version (`v0.0.70 → v0.0.75`) and outcome. Devices with running tasks are skipped and marked. Devices whose CLI is not connected or not remotely maintainable (foreground `lh connect`, Windows) are skipped, with the manual `lh update` command shown.
- Each requested device is followed through the existing `getCliUpdateState` until a new CLI process reports the target version, using the same success rule as the single-device panel. Rows whose restart is not confirmed within five minutes show as "Not confirmed". **Check again** re-plans from fresh device state; that is the retry path for failed and unconfirmed rows. Closing the dialog does not stop updates already sent.
- en-US and zh-CN copy written by hand; other locales come from the i18n workflow.

Screenshots and a recording will come with the acceptance round.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

Unit and router tests cover outcome classification, the re-check-before-restart rule, a restart whose acknowledgement was lost (followed, not failed), a device that was already running someone else's operation, permission and visibility filtering, gateway-only connections, input validation (duplicates, non-UUID request ids, unknown fields), and the client state machine (only ready devices targeted, polling stops per device once it settles, the five-minute timeout, recovery after a failed send). `bun run check` reports lint clean, 162 related tests passing, and type-check clean for the changed files. The lobe-design lint reports 0 FAIL / 0 WARN.

Not yet verified on the real product: devices actually restarting and reconnecting on a new version.

- Acceptance: Pending. The author will run product acceptance on a workspace with devices running an older `lh connect --daemon` and add the link here before merge.

Pre-deploy check: `updateClis` makes two device RPCs per target (check, then restart, each with a 15s timeout) with up to 8 in flight. For typical pool sizes this finishes in seconds, but confirm the lambda function's duration limit covers large pools. If the function is cut off mid-batch, devices already restarted still finish, and the dialog offers **Check again**.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None.

comment.body: @codex review latest code

Fixed in 9b6fc26a80. The per-request limit is now a shared constant, `DEVICE_CLI_BATCH_MAX_TARGETS` (50), in `@lobechat/types`. The router validates against it, and the modal sends ready devices in chunks of that size and merges the results. Each chunk is independent: if one request fails, only its devices are marked failed with the reason, the other chunks keep being followed, and **Check again** re-plans from the devices' real state. A regression test covers a pool of limit + 3, with the second chunk failing.

issue.title: ✨ feat(channel): notify members mentioned in a Channel message
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

When someone @-mentions other people in a workspace Channel message, the mentioned people can now be notified.

- `ChannelService.send` hands the stored message to a new helper, `notifyChannelMentions`. After the response, it resolves the message's `mentions` (channel member ids) to the Channel's **active human members**, then drops Agents, departed members and the sender. It calls a new business slot, `notifyChannelMention` (`src/business/server/channel-mention/notifyActivity.ts`), which is a no-op by default.
- Personal Channels and messages without mentions are skipped. The lookup runs through `after()` and only logs on failure, so a notification problem never fails or slows a send. It is scheduled right after the message is committed, before Agent scheduling, so a later queue failure does not drop the ping. A retried send returns the same message id, so implementations can dedupe per message.
- Mentions inside a human quote (which never dispatch Agents) still notify the quoted people. The mention is a direct ping either way.
- `channelPath` moves from `src/features/Channels/paths.ts` to `@lobechat/const` as `CHANNEL_URL`, so server-side links to a Channel/Thread share the SPA's route shape. `matchChannel` stays where it was. Behavior is unchanged.
- Adds the `channel_mentioned` / `channel_mentioned_title` notification copy and the `notification.item.channel_mentioned` settings label. en-US and zh-CN are written by hand; other locales are left to the daily auto-i18n workflow. `bun run i18n` was not run locally because no translation API key was available.

Heads-up:

- On desktop, the existing workspace mention watcher (`WorkspaceMentionNotifier`) already shows OS banners for unread `mention`-category inbox rows. A deployment that delivers this slot into that category gets the desktop banner with no client change, under the watcher's existing limits: active workspace only, window hidden or unfocused, ~30s poll.

#### Test

- [ ] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

- `mention.test.ts`: recipients are the mentioned people minus the sender, de-duplicated. Scheduling happens after the response. Personal Channels and empty mentions are skipped. Mentions of only Agents or the sender stay silent. Lookup failures never surface.
- `ChannelService.test.ts`: mentioned people are pinged once the message is stored, even when Agent scheduling then fails.
- `url.test.ts`: the `CHANNEL_URL` cases moved from `paths.test.ts`.
- `bun run check` (lint + related tests, 99 passed) and `bun run check --type` are clean.

- Acceptance: Pending. The author will verify on the real product (a teammate @-mentions the user in a workspace Channel; the inbox row and desktop banner appear and open the Channel/Thread) and add the link here.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None.

comment.body: @codex review latest code

Fixed in 8b5ab3a89c: recipients are now joined to non-deleted `workspace_members` of the Channel workspace, so a departed member whose Channel row stays active is skipped. Added `mention.db.test.ts` against real PostgreSQL; the departed-member case fails before this change and passes after.

Fixed in `10fd6c6850` (with the related option-forwarding correction in `4f92e4f6a5`). I chose the suggested safe-rejection path: before SIGTERM, `stopDaemonAndWait()` checks actual PID/PPID ancestry and refuses calls from the target daemon's own terminal/shell, with local-terminal/SSH guidance. An unavailable/incomplete ancestry check also refuses without stopping the connection; daemon identity is revalidated after the async check.

Real Linux PTY acceptance reproduced the old offline failure; the fixed PTY and shell cases preserve the connection. issue.title: 🩹 hotfix: backport auto approve and automatic release publication for v2.3.1
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

**Hotfix Scope:** v2.3.0 → v2.3.1. Backport the approval-card auto-approve action and the release-publication CI fix to `main`, without releasing the rest of `canary`.

This branch starts at the delivered `v2.3.0` tag and contains exactly two cherry-picked commits (with upstream provenance):

- #22122 — `51247c9152611cf1ee07b479a26de525f2677f7c`: add **Switch to auto approve** to the approval card, persist the preference before approval, and apply it to server continuations. Calls requiring explicit approval remain gated; share visitors cannot change the owner's mode. Also fixes the legacy edited-arguments path reloading pending rows, which could bring back a clickable approval card and interrupt the run on a second submission.
- #22069 — `064b15c538e6ca434ad3115e6757ab19126feed7`: explicitly pass the App token through `with.token` to release publication actions. This fixes the runner-token fallback that prevented downstream release workflows from starting.

Before/after screenshots and recordings are available in the reused upstream acceptance linked below. No new UI implementation or dependency changes were added in this backport.

#### Desktop sources

- Delivered baseline: `v2.3.0`.
- Base OSS: `700c8349e35477cb602975f8089c942e96bc9601`.
- Inherited Cloud revision: `88e1acf9ffc686a650c52b4911484992cfcbbf8e` (unchanged from the delivered baseline, not Cloud HEAD).
- Baseline delivery/source records were checked with the repository's hotfix-intent CLI.

<!-- desktop-release-request {"schemaVersion":1,"mode":"hotfix","baseVersion":"2.3.0","cloudSha":"88e1acf9ffc686a650c52b4911484992cfcbbf8e","baseSourcesHash":"7b7eb9d4909823087e4e0193befe577e67c993de25d6709c6ae6f618193dd84b"} -->

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests (carried from #22122)
- Changed-file `bun run check --lint --test --type`: **86 tests passed**, lint and types clean.
- Before/after regression check: the two legacy-resume regression tests fail with the v2.3.0 implementations; restoring this backport makes all **55 tests** in the two affected store suites pass.
- Release-workflow lint passed; `node --test .github/scripts/desktopRelease*.test.mjs`: **61 passed**.
- `git diff --check` passed. The auto-approve backport's patch ID matches its upstream commit.
- Acceptance: https://lobehub.com/acceptance/7e75521b-766a-442e-9fa3-5a7ed89b7b59
  - Reusing the upstream evidence, not claiming a fresh packaged-Stable acceptance run: **8/9 criteria passed**, with required evidence present for those eight. This covers the approval-card layout, mode persistence, same-run continuation, high-risk gating, and duplicate-submission fixes.
  - **Known gap:** the Cloud approval-takeover continuation criterion remains uncertain; its required video is missing, and only unit tests cover that path. This backport does not claim to close that gap.
  - The CI-only token wiring change needs no additional product acceptance; its upstream before/after action-bundle probe is documented in #22069.

#### Release process

1. Wait for the release bot to bump `package.json` to the next stable patch (expected **2.3.1**, while v2.3.0 remains the latest stable tag).
2. Merge into `main` after required checks/review. Auto Tag validates the pinned source metadata and creates the stable tag and GitHub Release.
3. The published Release triggers Desktop Stable and Docker publication. Confirm their successful completion and installer/update-feed delivery; creation of a tag alone is not proof of delivery.
4. The next eligible Canary run calculates its version from the new stable tag (expected **2.3.2-canary.1**) and performs a full release when the old Canary shell has been overtaken.

No merge, workflow dispatch, or production release was performed while preparing this PR.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Backports #22122 and #22069. No separate matching issue is claimed.

Verified with a component test that failed before the change (no people checkbox rendered) and passed after it. Per the repo testing rule against new component tests, it is not committed, and this render-boundary fix has no hook logic to extract.

issue.title: ✨ feat: support Antigravity local agents
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Add Antigravity (`agy`) as a local heterogeneous agent across CLI and Desktop, with remote-device execution available from the Web UI. The native stream-json adapter handles conversation resume, tool calls/results, per-step token and cache usage, and actionable CLI errors. Runs use YOLO permissions by default.

- Discover complete model variants from `agy models` on the execution device. Each variant includes its thinking level, so the picker has no separate effort selector.
- Relay native `/usage` snapshots through the device gateway and display their model groups, remaining quota, reset times, and refresh state. Preserve native bucket semantics; AI Credits are excluded.
- Add CLI discovery, shared device handlers, Desktop IPC, Web controls, and English/Chinese strings.

Screenshots of the model picker, tool results, usage details and quota panel, plus a sampled continuation recording, are included in the acceptance report below. Structured in-run user questions are outside this change.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed
- Related lint and tests passed, including 173 checks after the model-variant fix and 78 quota-related tests during implementation. The CLI build passed.
- Full-repository type-check remains blocked by existing diagnostics/dependency gaps; affected-file filtering found no diagnostics in the changed files. Some frontend/server suites could not load missing workspace dependencies in the local environment.
- Acceptance: https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/dc03fc2a-5e71-4693-bcd3-cc6a7e9c7bca — **5/5 checks passed** on the deployed Web build and a connected macOS CLI device. Covers device routing, model selection, real tool execution and continuation, token/cache usage, and live quota refresh. Native agy startup logs corroborate both tested model variants. The second round supplements existing evidence without rerunning the model tests.
- Acceptance limits: the deployed revision was user-attested; the sampled recording shows continuation submission/loading, with completion supported by a screenshot and native transcript. Desktop-specific behavior was not exercised in this Web/device run.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Related to #20230.

issue.title: 💄 style(conversation): move topic Share into the header menu inside workspaces
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Inside a workspace, the topic header showed both **Comments** and **Share**. For teammates, Share is mostly the wrong tool: they can already open the topic, and the popover's main action publishes an external `/share/t/<id>` link (which may be limited to the agent creator / workspace owners). Internal collaboration happens through comments. This PR keeps the header focused on comments in workspaces and moves Share one level down.

- **Workspace**: the desktop header `ShareButton` (agent conversation) no longer renders; the comment button takes the slot. The mobile chat header keeps its Share button: it has no `...` menu, so the button stays the only entry to the link-sharing popover there. The `...` topic menu gains a **Share** item, first in the copy/open group, which opens the same `SharePopover` (link toggle, copy link, export entry) anchored under the `...` button.
- **Personal**: unchanged. The header Share button stays and the menu gets no Share item.
- Same behavior as the old header button: without link sharing (`enableBusinessFeatures` off) the item opens the export modal directly; users without `edit_own_content` see it disabled.
- `SharePopover` accepts optional `open` / `onOpenChange` / `anchor` / `placement` so it can be opened programmatically; existing callers are unaffected.
- The popover opens on the menu's `onOpenChangeComplete`. The menu returns focus to its trigger as it closes, and a popover opened any earlier reads that as focus-out and dismisses itself.
- Group chat headers are untouched (they have no comment button).

Before/after screenshots and a recording of the menu → popover flow are in the acceptance round below (workspace scope only renders in the Cloud build).

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

`ShareButton` hides on desktop in a workspace, still renders in personal scope, and still renders on mobile in a workspace (each new case fails without its change). `HeaderActions` drives the real `DropdownMenu`: the Share item opens the popover after the menu closes, falls back to the export modal without link sharing, and is absent in personal scope. `useMenu` places Share before the copy/open actions only when provided. Lint is clean; the touched test files pass (16 tests). `bun run type-check` reports only the two errors in `src/layout/GlobalProvider/fontFamilyOverride.ts` that also appear on this branch without these changes.

The existing `ShareButton` test mocked `next/dynamic`, but the component loads through `@/libs/next/dynamic`, so that mock never applied; it now mocks `@/features/SharePopover/lazy` directly.

- Acceptance: https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/8bc53b43-7166-4cb2-9864-7c8b9caf4e77 — 7/7 checks pass, all required evidence uploaded. Run on a local Cloud runtime with the OSS submodule at the base (`1c08e91e94`) and at this PR head (`4af9f3fc84`). Covered: the workspace header loses Share and comments take its slot; the `...` menu gains Share above Copy Topic ID (also 分享 in zh-CN); choosing it opens the popover under `...`, which stays open after mouse and keyboard activation (chaptered recording); the link switch and Export row work, and Export opens the export dialog; Escape and outside-click dismissal, then reopening; personal scope is unchanged before/after; on a phone viewport a workspace topic still reaches Share from `...`. An independent checker reviewed all media. Not covered: business features off, the `edit_own_content` disabled state, and the link-publish restriction for non-owners.
- Note on the mobile guard: on Cloud, workspace routes on phones render the desktop agent layout, which carries the `...` menu, so the mobile `ChatHeader` only appears outside workspaces. The `!mobile` guard is defensive and keeps that header's Share entry if it is ever shown in a workspace.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

None.

comment.body: @codex review

Good catch, fixed in 4af9f3fc84. The workspace hiding now applies only to the desktop header (`if (workspaceId && !mobile) return null`). The mobile chat header keeps its Share button, since it has no `...` menu to host the relocated entry. Added a regression test: `ShareButton mobile` still renders inside a workspace. It fails without the fix.

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'avatar')
    at app://renderer/assets/AgentTool-HJ42Y6s8.js:4:3725
    at xo (app://renderer/vendor/vendor-react-main_overlay_popup-BtXe-Or7.js:8:47496)
    at mc (...:8:69994)
    at oc (...:8:67412)
    at ac (...:8:66965)
    at jc (...:8:82648)
    at Mu (...:8:115653)
    at ku (...:8:114734)
    at Ou (...:8:114572)
    at gu (...:8:111439)
```

### 📷 How to reproduce it?

1. Open any agent (or 助理档案 for Lobe AI / a workspace agent).
2. The profile page fails immediately and deterministically — it is not agent-specific.

### 🚦 What it should be?

The agent profile opens normally (Identity header + runtime config + tools).

### 📝 Additional Information

The failing chunk is the profile editor's tools area (`src/features/ProfileEditor/AgentTool.tsx`, which also pulls in `PluginTag.tsx`). Two call sites read `.meta.avatar` without a guard:

- `src/features/ProfileEditor/AgentTool.tsx` — `avatar={item.meta.avatar}` over `filteredBuiltinList` (chip + popover icon)
- `src/features/ProfileEditor/PluginTag.tsx` — `avatar: builtinMeta.meta.avatar` inside the `localMeta` memo
- the same latent pattern exists in `src/features/ToolTag/index.tsx`

`LobeToolMeta.meta` is already marked `@deprecated` (identity is being hoisted to the top level), and the equivalently-derived list in `src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Tools/useControls.tsx` reads `item.meta?.avatar`. So a single meta-less entry takes down the whole profile page while the chat input tolerates it.

Suggested fix — fall back to the hoisted identity once, in `toBuiltinMeta` (`src/store/tool/slices/builtin/selectors.ts`):

```ts
meta: t.manifest.meta ?? { avatar: t.avatar, title: t.title, description: t.description },
```

and/or guard the two reads above with `item.meta?.avatar`.

Follow-up worth checking: every builtin-tool manifest in this repo carries `meta`, so the meta-less entry may come from a registry that adds tools at runtime / at deploy time — worth finding the exact identifier so the manifest can be fixed at the source.

### 🛠️ Willing to Submit a PR?

Yes, I am willing to submit a PR

issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Channel conversations repeat identity headers and wide spacing for consecutive short messages, while long previews interrupt scanning. Group adjacent messages from the same actor within five minutes, preserve identity at day/join/thread/reply boundaries, and tighten continuation spacing.

Long text now collapses to a 160 px preview with full expansion; attachments remain visible independently. Localized clocks and date separators make timing easier to follow, and continuation actions use a dedicated icon lane to avoid covering text. After integrating canary's quoted replies, compact rows provide labelled Reply and Start thread icons with space reserved for both actions, and retain quote navigation and highlighting.

Before/after screenshots are available in the [acceptance report](https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/4ad0808b-0394-4bb8-9e5a-daf90d2f4d16) (CR-01 for grouping, CR-03 for long-text previews).

- `bun run check --lint --test --type` passed after rebasing onto canary, including 42 related page/channel tests and the repository type check.

The three `no-unguarded-response-field` errors in `ChannelMessage.tsx` are false positives, so no fallback was added:

issue.title: 🐛 fix(channel): send responders unseen recent context as tagged blocks
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

A Channel responder used to get only the triggering request, serialized as JSON. That broke follow-ups such as "two is a bit early, how about three?": unless the responder had made the earlier proposal itself, it had to call the history tools to learn what "two" referred to. That cannot work when the request says "don't call tools", and it costs a round trip on every follow-up. The JSON also put user/agent ids and a request id in front of the model, even though the instructions tell it not to volunteer ids. It escaped the user's text, and it wrapped a single message in an array.

**Recent context, bounded to what the topic has not seen**
- New `ChannelExecutionRepository.recentContext`. It returns at most 5 public messages before the request, from the same branch as the history tools (`readManifestMessages`): everything after the last request the run's topic accepted, minus the reply that topic published. A new topic gets the latest 5. Anything older stays behind `lobe-channel.readMessages` / `lh channel history`.
- `input` retains canary’s current request and explicit quote, preserving attachment resolution and isolation; recent context is fetched separately.

**Tagged request instead of JSON**

```
<channel_message from="Coder" type="agent" boundary="3fa9c1d2e0b4">
Two o'clock?
</channel_message boundary="3fa9c1d2e0b4">
<channel_request from="Mia" type="user" to="Codex" boundary="3fa9c1d2e0b4">
Two is a bit early, how about three?
</channel_request boundary="3fa9c1d2e0b4">
```

- Every tag carries a random per-run `boundary`, so a tag quoted inside a message cannot close a block or forge an author. JSON escaping used to give this protection. Attribute values are escaped.
- An optional `channel_quote` block preserves explicit replies (up to 6000 characters) and is deduplicated from recent context. It uses the same boundary as the other blocks.
- No ids, except on a block a tool call has to expand. Context excerpts are capped at 2000 characters and marked `truncated`. Blocks with attachments carry an `attachments` count. External runtimes are handed only images, so for them this count replaces the request's old `fileIds` as the way to learn about other files.
- `CHANNEL_INSTRUCTIONS`, the native `lobe-channel` system role and both Channel READMEs describe the new shape.

**Reply-scope rule** (first commit): the "who is a participant" rules from #21899, including a hard-coded example exchange, are replaced with one general rule: match the answer to the scope of the question. The constraints they enforced (no dossier of past messages, directories or tasks; no unrelated agents or workspace inventory; no unrequested offers) now apply to every question.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

- `topicContinuation.test.ts`: a new topic receives the latest 5 messages. A continued topic receives only the message posted after its previous request, without its own published reply.
- `channel.test.ts`: exact rendering of context + request blocks without ids; ids and markers only on truncated or attachment-bearing blocks (request included); forged closing tags and quoted names stay inside their block.
- After resolving the canary merge: lint clean, 85 related tests pass, and the full repository type-check passes.
- Added quote regressions for the 6000-character limit, attribution, boundary protection, and deduplication with recent context; the two affected cases failed before the resolution and passed after it.

- Acceptance: [Local Channel verification](https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/db073769-f8d6-402b-a604-02912be83303) — six outcomes exercised successfully on the local branch: native and Codex first-topic recent-context follow-ups without tools, native topic continuation, targeted identity replies on both runtimes, and an explicit quote outside the recent-five window. Independent evidence review passed. **Publication is partial because account storage quota blocked most evidence uploads**; only two inline text evidence records were retained; all six required screenshots and the remaining text evidence are missing remotely. All 12 artifacts are retained in a complete local offline report, so remote required-evidence coverage is incomplete.
- Conflict resolution commit: `c828c8cf5b` (canary `9a85ab5bf4`). Delivered head `9b9ce6a681` adds only a StyleX lint allowlist update; it does not invalidate the product verification.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

Follow-up to #21545 and #21899.

issue.title: ✨ feat(channel): open a General channel with each new project
issue.body:
### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

New projects now open with a default **General** Channel, so the Channel sidebar of a fresh project is no longer empty.

- **Flag gate**: created only while the `channel` runtime flag is on for the project creator. Users outside the beta get nothing new.
- **Members**: the creator (owner) plus the project's main agent.
  - An external main agent (Claude Code, Codex, …) needs a device and working directory, which only a member can pick. In that case the scope's LobeAI joins instead, so the first message in General always gets an answer. The external agent can be added with a device afterwards.
- **Best-effort**: the project already exists, so any failure is logged with its ids and never fails `project.create`.
- **Client**: when the flag is on, the project store refetches the Channel list right after creating a project, so the new Channel appears without waiting for the 60s idle poll.

Implementation:

- `apps/server/src/services/channel/defaultChannel.ts`: `createDefaultChannel` holds the flag gate, the fixed `General` title and the error logging. It takes an optional `workspaceId`, so a workspace-scoped default Channel can reuse it.
- `ChannelService.createDefault`: seats the main agent when it is native, otherwise the scope's LobeAI. It never opens an agent-less Channel, whose messages would go unanswered with no feedback. Runtime detection is shared with `resolveAgent` through a small `agentRuntime` helper.
- `project.create` calls the helper after the project row exists.
- Fix found during acceptance: `requireChannelAgent` now normalizes the inbox title. Before, a LobeAI member was stored with the name "Agent", because builtin inbox rows have no title; this affected every Channel LobeAI joins, not only General. Members added earlier keep their stored name; there is no backfill.
- Fix from Codex review: `ProjectModel.isDedicatedCoordinator` now counts an active Channel membership as "still used". Before, replacing the main agent of a project created without a chosen one deleted its generated coordinator, the agent seated in General, which left General without an agent. Project deletion uses the same check, so a Channel that outlives its project keeps its agent too.

#### Test

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] No tests needed

New unit tests:

- `defaultChannel.test.ts`: flag off, workspace and project scopes, failures swallowed with ids.
- `ChannelService.default.test.ts`: a native agent is seated; an external, heterogeneous-provider or unreachable agent falls back to LobeAI; with no usable agent at all, no Channel is opened.
- `project.create.test.ts`: the resolved main agent is passed in the caller's scope.
- `store.test.ts`: the Channel list is refetched only while the flag is on.
- `agentMember.test.ts` (real PostgreSQL): adding LobeAI records its product name. The test fails without the fix.
- `projectCoordinator/__tests__/index.test.ts` (real PostgreSQL): a replaced coordinator that answers in a Channel is kept, along with its membership. The test fails without the fix.

`bun run check` passes: lint clean, 185 related tests. `bun run check --type` is clean.

- Acceptance: https://app.lobehub.com/acceptance/1c2e176f-4166-42d2-939a-deffae444c2c
  - Round 1 (7/7): verified on an isolated Cloud build of this branch, with one flag-on user and one flag-off user.
    - General is created for a new workspace, a workspace project, a project with a custom native main agent, a project with an external (`claude-code`) main agent (LobeAI fallback), and a personal project.
    - The list refreshes without a reload: `channel.list` refetched 1.7 s after `project.create`.
    - With the flag off, no channel is created and `channel.list` returns 403.
    - With channel creation forced to fail, the workspace and project are still created and the failure is logged with ids.
    - An independent checker inspected all 24 screenshots and the text evidence.
  - Round 2 (1/1): after the fix, the LobeAI member in a new General reads "Lobe AI" instead of "Agent", shown as a before/after pair.
  - Not covered by acceptance: the coordinator-replacement fix (c7bd7e22a2) landed after both rounds. It is verified by its real-PostgreSQL regression test only.

#### 🔗 Related Issue

N/A
